decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 3%.

changes.quote: FOMC statement: Federal Reserve and other central banks announce specific measures designed to address liquidity pressures in funding markets
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Since the coordinated actions taken in December 2007, the G-10 central banks have continued to work together closely and to consult regularly on liquidity pressures in funding markets.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Pressures in some of these markets have recently increased again.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: We all continue to work together and will take appropriate steps to address those liquidity pressures.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: To that end, today the Bank of Canada, the Bank of England, the European Central Bank, the Federal Reserve, and the Swiss National Bank are announcing specific measures.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The Federal Reserve announced today an expansion of its securities lending program.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.75% APR costs about $53.12 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.6% and moved +14 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.24% would rise by about $27.39 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.9%, and employers added an average of 13k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.1% over the past year (February 2008); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +27 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.04% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 21%, cut 0%, hike 79%.
validation_notes: Statement does not state a target; showing the prevailing target from FRED.
